reasons.text: The museum presented Naegeli's artistic work beyond his graffiti and organized exhibitions dedicated to him.
reasons.quote: Erstmals wird Harald Naegeli nicht in erster Linie für seine Werke im öffentlichen Raum, sondern als vielseitiger, unbekannter stiller Schaffer gewürdigt.

reasons.quote: Hugo Ball, Emmy Hennings, Hans Arp, Marcel Janco, Richard Huelsenbeck and Tristan Tzara founded the Cabaret Voltaire in Spiegelgasse 1 – and the Dada movement with it.

reasons.text: James Joyce fled to Zurich from Trieste during the First World War with his family and lived at this address.
reasons.quote: Following the outbreak of the First World War, Joyce flees from Trieste to Zurich, along with his future wife Nora Barnacle and their children Giorgio and Lucia.

reasons.quote: A commemorative plaque can be seen at Universitätsstrasse 38, one of the places where Joyce and his family live.

reasons.quote: Writers from abroad in Zurich

reasons.quote: Zurich is more than just home to great authors such as Gottfried Keller and Max Frisch: it has frequently been a destination, stopping-off point, refuge or adopted home for writers from abroad who came to the city seeking inspiration or protection, stayed for varying lengths of time, and even died here.

reasons.text: The exhibition covered writers escaping fascism and war in the twentieth century.
reasons.quote: while in the 20th a whole series of literary figures sought shelter from the ravages of war and Fascism.

reasons.text: Lenin lived in Spiegelgasse while preparing for the Russian Revolution.

reasons.text: The street brought together political revolutionaries and artistic avant-garde figures.
reasons.quote: Europe's artistic and political avant-garde met at the Spiegelgasse at the beginning of the 20th century.

reasons.text: The institution documents the life and work of James Joyce, whose Zurich years formed part of his life in exile.
reasons.quote: For Joyce, Zurich is one among a number of homes in exile.

places.name: Wellenberg Prison Tower
places.address: Former Wellenberg prison tower, Limmat, Zürich

reasons.text: The tower imprisoned and tortured people accused of witchcraft, including the eight defendants in the last Zurich witch trial in 1701.
reasons.quote: Die acht Menschen wurden verhaftet, in den Gefängnisturm Wellenberg überführt und aufs Schwerste gefoltert, bis sie gestanden, sich mit dem Teufel eingelassen zu haben.

reasons.text: The Wellenberg tower was used by the authorities as a prison for accused witches and as a place of torture.
reasons.quote: Sie wurden von den staatlichen Behörden in den Wellenberg-Turm gesperrt und der «Kleine Rat» übernahm als Malefizrat, als Strafgericht.

places.name: Limmat River – execution site of Agatha Studler

reasons.text: Agatha Studler, the only victim of witch persecution from the city of Zurich, was drowned in the Limmat in 1546.
reasons.quote: Angeklagte, die dem Vorwurf der Teufelsbuhlschaft entgehen konnten, wurden in der Limmat ertränkt. So z. B. auch Agatha Studler, das einzige Stadtzürcher Opfer der Hexenverfolgung.

reasons.text: The historical account describes the drowning of Agatha Studler in the river.
reasons.quote: As she prayed for mercy, she was drowned instead of burnt.

reasons.text: People convicted of witchcraft were burned alive on a gravel bank of the Sihl.
reasons.quote: Die Verurteilten wurden bei lebendigem Leibe auf einer Kiesbank der Sihl verbrannt, in späteren Jahren wurden sie vermehrt gnadenhalber zuvor enthauptet.

places.name: Zurich City Hall and the Kleine Rat

reasons.text: The Kleine Rat acted as the criminal court responsible for witchcraft cases.
reasons.quote: Der Kleine Rat, der gleichzeitig Regierung, Parlament und Gerichtshof des Stadtstaats Zürich fungierte, setzte sich aus 48 Ratsherren aus den Zünften und der Gesellschaft zur Constaffel (der früheren Zürcher Oberschicht) zusammen.

reasons.text: The court used torture and confession as instruments of prosecution.
reasons.quote: Ein Schuldbekenntnis war die Voraussetzung für die Vergebung der Sünden.

reasons.text: The army violently dispersed a demonstration at Münsterplatz on 10 November 1918. Three workers were injured and one soldier died.
reasons.quote: Am Tag darauf löste die Armee eine Demonstration auf dem Zürcher Münsterplatz gewaltsam auf. Drei Arbeiter wurden verletzt, ein Soldat starb.

reasons.text: During the military occupation of Zurich in November 1918, the cantonal government moved its headquarters to the barracks and held its meetings under military protection.
reasons.quote: Gleichzeitig verlegte der Zürcher Regierungsrat seinen Sitz in die Kaserne, wo er unter Militärschutz tagte.

reasons.text: The military occupation of Zurich was a decisive event leading to the national general strike.
reasons.quote: Die militärische Besetzung Zürichs 1918 löste den nationalen Landesstreik aus, die schwerste politische Krise des Bundesstaats.

places.name: Zurich city centre – military occupation and street patrols
places.address: Central Zurich, including bridges, streets and administrative buildings

reasons.text: Military troops were stationed at public buildings, banks, bridges and street intersections during the occupation.
reasons.quote: Soldaten wurden vor Amts- und Dienstgebäuden, Banken, Konsulaten, auf Brücken und Strassenkreuzungen postiert und fuhren mit aufgepflanzten Bajonetten auf den Plattformen der Strassenbahnen mit.

reasons.text: The military presence was widespread throughout the city.
reasons.quote: Die Präsenz des Militärs in Zürich war allgegenwärtig.

places.name: Zurich financial district – banks and Paradeplatz

reasons.text: Banks were among the locations occupied by military personnel during the crisis.

places.name: Zurich – workers' movement and general strike

reasons.text: The strike movement was driven by workers' opposition to political marginalization, poor wages and shortages.
reasons.quote: Die gewerkschaftlich organisierte Arbeiterschaft und einzelne Angestelltenverbände wehrten sich in verschiedenen zeitlich und örtlich begrenzten Streiks gegen ihre politische Marginalisierung.

reasons.text: The general strike included demands for the 48-hour working week, women's suffrage and social insurance.
reasons.quote: Einführung des Frauenstimmrechts

reasons.text: The strike was a major turning point for the Swiss labour movement.
reasons.quote: Obwohl der Landesstreik einer Niederlage der Arbeiterschaft gleichkam, ging sie langfristig doch gestärkt daraus hervor.

reasons.text: The Fraumünster was founded as a convent for women in 853.
reasons.quote: Founded in 853 by King Louis the German, this church with its convent was inhabited by the female members of the aristocracy of Europe.

reasons.text: The abbesses exercised considerable political and economic power, including the right to mint coins.
reasons.quote: The convent enjoyed the patronage of kings and the abbess the right to mint coins in Zurich until well into the 13th century.

reasons.text: The abbey was an important centre of power in medieval Zurich.
reasons.quote: In addition, the incumbent abbess was the official ruler of Zurich from the 13th century onwards, holding the title of royal princess.

reasons.text: According to Zurich's historical legend, women defended the city against an attacking army in 1292.
reasons.quote: In 1292, with the city under siege, Zürich's women are said to have lined the Lindenhof in armour and turned the attackers away.

reasons.text: The location is a key stop on the walking tour dedicated to women who shaped Zurich.
reasons.quote: The hilltop where the women of Zürich are said to have saved the city in 1292.

reasons.text: The University of Zurich was one of the first universities in Europe to admit women, beginning in 1866.
reasons.quote: Lange Zeit waren Frauen vom Hochschulstudium ausgeschlossen, bis die Universität Zürich 1866 nach der Universität Sorbonne in Paris als eine der ersten Hochschulen in Europa Frauen zum Studium zuließ.

reasons.text: Nadeschda Suslowa became the first woman to earn a doctorate in the German-speaking world at Zurich.
reasons.quote: In Zürich promovierte sie 1867 als erste Frau im deutschsprachigen Raum und legte im folgenden Jahr in Russland als erste Frau das russische Staatsexamen ab.

reasons.text: The university honours Nadeschda Suslowa with a commemorative plaque in its main building.
reasons.quote: In einer feierlichen Zeremonie wurde der Pionierin im Juli 2020 im Hauptgebäude der UZH eine Gedenktafel gewidmet.

reasons.text: Emilie Kempin-Spyri became the first female lecturer at the university.

reasons.text: The monument commemorates Emilie Kempin-Spyri, a pioneer of women's equality and the first woman to obtain habilitation in the German-speaking world.

reasons.text: She practised medicine here from 1874 until her final illness.

reasons.quote: Bis heute gilt die “Pflegi” als Symbol für die Reform des Pflegeberufes, als Andenken an die bürgerliche Frauenbewegung und formt einen Teil Zürcher Stadtgeschichte.

places.name: Former Hauser & Biedermann Silk Twisting Mill

reasons.text: The site preserves a nineteenth-century silk-twisting factory and associated factory owner's residence.
reasons.quote: Das Fabrikgebäude der Seidenzwirnerei Hauser & Biedermann und das zugehörige Fabrikantenwohnhaus entstanden um 1865 anstelle einer älteren Pulvermühle.

reasons.text: The owners operated additional silk-processing and production businesses.
reasons.quote: Die Seidenhersteller Hauser & Biedermann waren im Besitz weiterer Betriebe in der Seidenverarbeitung und -produktion.

reasons.text: The preserved industrial complex is recognised as evidence of Zurich's industrial history.
reasons.quote: Das gut erhaltene Industrieensemble samt Kanalabschnitt ist ein Zeuge der Industriegeschichte der Stadt Zürich.

reasons.text: The villa's owner was a tobacco and plantation entrepreneur whose wealth was connected to overseas trade, providing a useful comparative perspective on the global economic connections of Zurich's industrial bourgeoisie.
reasons.quote: The merchant Carl Fürchtegott Grob had Villa Patumbah built in 1885 by the well-known Zurich architects Alfred Chiodera and Theophil Tschudy.

reasons.text: The park became an internationally notorious open drug scene during the 1980s and early 1990s.
reasons.quote: Unfortunately, the park gained notoriety in the 1990s when it became a meeting place for drug addicts from all over the world.

reasons.text: Thousands of drug users and dealers gathered there daily.
reasons.quote: At times, up to 3,000 dealers and drug users gathered in the Platzspitz every day.

reasons.text: The site became internationally known as Needle Park.
reasons.quote: These tragic circumstances led to it becoming known internationally as “Needle Park”.

reasons.text: The closure and redevelopment of the park in 1992 marked a significant turning point in Zurich's drug policy.
reasons.quote: 1992: Der Platzspitz wird geschlossen.

places.name: Oberer Letten (former Letten railway station and open drug scene)

reasons.text: The Letten area became the successor to the Platzspitz open drug scene after the park closed.
reasons.quote: However, addicts then congregated on the site of the unused Letten train station (now Oberer Letten), where the open drug scene continued until 1995.

reasons.text: The city experienced a second major open drug scene at the former railway station.
reasons.quote: 1993: Es bildet sich eine neue offene Drogenszene am stillgelegten Bahnhof Letten.

reasons.text: The closure of the Letten drug scene marked a decisive moment in the transformation of Zurich's addiction policy.
reasons.quote: 1995: Die offene Drogenszene am Letten wird geschlossen.

reasons.text: Zurich introduced controlled consumption rooms as a harm-reduction measure in 1987.
reasons.quote: 1987: Das Sozialdepartement eröffnet «Fixerstübli» (kontrollierte Konsumräume), um die gesundheitlichen Risiken des Drogenkonsums zu reduzieren und die öffentliche Ordnung zu wahren.

reasons.text: The initial facilities operated in converted trolleybuses at changing locations.
reasons.quote: Vorerst sind die «Fixerstübli» in umgebauten Trolleybussen mit wechselnden Standorten.

places.name: Zurich's drug-policy history (municipal policy and harm-reduction development)

reasons.text: Zurich introduced a four-pillar drug policy combining prevention, treatment, harm reduction and repression in 1994.
reasons.quote: 1994: Einführung des Vier-Säulen-Modells (Prävention, Therapie, Schadensminderung, Repression).

reasons.text: The four-pillar model became the foundation of Zurich's drug policy.
reasons.quote: Das Vier-Säulen-Modell wird zur Grundlage der Zürcher Drogenpolitik.

reasons.text: Zurich experimented with controlled heroin distribution in the early 1990s.
reasons.quote: 1993: Erste Versuche kontrollierter Heroinabgabe.

reasons.text: The venue was founded in 1916 by Hugo Ball and Emmy Hennings and became the birthplace of Dada.
reasons.quote: Hugo Ball and Emmy Hennings founded the Cabaret Voltaire in the middle of Zurich’s Old Town in 1916.

reasons.text: Its performances brought together music, literature, dance and visual art.
reasons.quote: In the middle of the First World War, Dada awakened the desire to question the present with new and surprising forms of artistic performance, expressed through music, literature, dance, and painting.

reasons.text: It was a meeting place for musicians, performers and artists challenging conventional artistic forms.
reasons.quote: Artists, musicians, dancers and literati met here and called all existing forms of art into question.

reasons.text: The Tonhalle has been the home of the Tonhalle Orchestra since 1895.
reasons.quote: The Tonhalle Zürich has been the home of the Tonhalle-Orchester Zürich since 1895.

reasons.text: Its inauguration featured conductors Friedrich Hegar and Johannes Brahms.
reasons.quote: The inaugural concerts were conducted by Friedrich Hegar, Chief Conductor at the time, and the composer Johannes Brahms.

reasons.text: The orchestra's origins go back to the foundation of a permanent professional musical organisation in 1868.
reasons.quote: After the Swiss Music Festival held in Zurich in 1867, interested parties succeeded in harnessing audiences’ enthusiasm to found a public limited company in 1868 with the aim of promoting musical life with a permanent orchestra: the Tonhalle-Gesellschaft Zürich, which continues to support the Tonhalle-Orchester Zürich to this day and is organised as a public limited company.

reasons.text: The Opera House originated with the Aktientheater, which opened in 1834 with Mozart's The Magic Flute.
reasons.quote: The history of Zurich Opera House begins with the «Actien-Theater» (shares theatre), which opened in 1834 with Mozart’s «Zauberflöte».

reasons.text: The present building was inaugurated in 1891 with Wagner's Lohengrin.
reasons.quote: It was inaugurated with Wagner’s «Lohengrin» under the name of «Stadttheater» (town theatre) in 1891.

reasons.text: The institution has played an important role in Zurich's opera and orchestral history.
reasons.quote: Founding of the Tonhalle-Orchester Zürich, which played both symphonic concerts and operatic performances through 1944.

reasons.text: The original Aktientheater was an important performance venue where Richard Wagner conducted operas.
reasons.quote: Richard Wagner conducted performances here in the early 1850s, including his own Der fliegende Holländer and Tannhäuser.

reasons.text: The venue was the starting point of Zurich's permanent theatre and orchestral traditions.
reasons.quote: Zurich’s first permanent theatre, it was established in the form of a joint stock company by theatre-loving citizens.

reasons.text: Richard Wagner presented the first public reading of his complete Ring poem at the hotel.
reasons.quote: He also gave the first public reading of his complete Ring poem in the Hotel Baur au Lac.

reasons.text: The hotel was an important gathering place for Wagner and his musical and intellectual circle.
reasons.quote: The hotel was venue and meeting place of the Wagner circle for over seven years.

reasons.text: The Casino was Zurich's principal concert hall until 1867.
reasons.quote: until 1867 the only concert hall in Zurich

reasons.text: Richard Wagner conducted subscription concerts there between 1850 and 1855.
reasons.quote: Wagner directed numerous subscription concerts of the Allgemeine Musikgesellschaft (AMG) from 1850 to 1855, amongst others Beethoven’s symphonies, works of Weber, Mozart and Gluck.

reasons.text: Roman settlement and military fortification.
reasons.quote: Zuerst als keltische Siedlung nachgewiesen, wurde der Lindenhof ab 15 v. Chr. zum römischen Militärstützpunkt.

reasons.text: Remains of medieval royal palaces.
reasons.quote: Im Keller auf dem Lindenhof, einst Brennpunkt und Machtzentrum der städtischen Siedlung, können heute die Reste des römischen Kastells und der mittelalterlichen Königspfalz besichtigt werden.

reasons.text: Archaeological remains of medieval and Roman buildings.
reasons.quote: Im Mittelalter standen auf dem Lindenhof grosse Pfalzgebäude, in denen Könige und Kaiser residierten.

reasons.text: Roman tombstone recording the ancient name of Zurich, Turicum.
reasons.quote: To this day, a tombstone dating from 180 AD can be found on the way up to the Lindenhof.

reasons.text: Preserved archaeological remains of Roman thermal baths.
reasons.quote: In 1983, during renovation work on a toyshop, the remains of ancient Roman baths were discovered, thus putting Zürich's history in a new light.

reasons.text: The remains can be viewed in situ through a protective metal grating.
reasons.quote: The baths were excavated and can now be viewed around the clock through a metal grating.

reasons.text: Evidence of Roman public bathing and social life.
reasons.quote: The thermal baths were heated and formed a central meeting place for the public at large – at least until the Romans withdrew from Zürich in 405 / 406 A.D.

reasons.text: Archaeological remains from prehistoric pile-dwelling settlements and Zurich's earlier history.
reasons.quote: In so-called Archäologische Fenster (archaeological windows), the Department of City Planning shows treasures from Zurich’s past, such as the ruins of a Roman fort, the remains of prehistoric pile dwellings, and the Ehgraben sewer, which reveals how a medieval town dealt with its waste and sewage problems.

reasons.text: One of the publicly accessible archaeological exhibitions in the city.
reasons.quote: Most of these “windows” are open to the public free of charge – such as the one in the Parkhaus Opéra underground garage at Sechseläutenplatz and the small exhibition in the Thermengasse.

places.name: Ehgraben Archaeological Window
places.address: Ehgraben, Zurich Old Town, 8001 Zürich, Switzerland

reasons.text: Preserved medieval sewer illustrating medieval waste disposal and sanitation.
reasons.quote: In so-called Archäologische Fenster (archaeological windows), the Department of City Planning shows treasures from Zurich’s past, such as the ruins of a Roman fort, the remains of prehistoric pile dwellings, and the Ehgraben sewer, which reveals how a medieval town dealt with its waste and sewage problems.

reasons.text: The site provides evidence of medieval everyday life and urban infrastructure.
reasons.quote: Und ein Gang durch den schmalen Ehgraben zeigt, wie im Spätmittelalter mit Abfällen aus den Küchen und Latrinen entsorgt wurden.

reasons.text: Archaeological remains associated with a medieval Jewish house.
reasons.quote: The spectrum of archaeological windows ranges from the pile dwellers and the ruins of the Roman fort to a view of a medieval Jewish house and the moat, which illustrates the waste and sewage problems of a medieval town.

reasons.text: One of the designated archaeological windows in Zurich's Old Town.
reasons.quote: However, a key is needed to visit the Ehgraben, Lindenhof-Keller, Stadtmauerkeller, and Brunngasse.

reasons.text: Archaeological remains relating to the medieval city's fortifications.
reasons.quote: In so-called Archäologische Fenster (archaeological windows), the Department of City Planning shows treasures from Zurich’s past, such as the ruins of a Roman fort, the remains of prehistoric pile dwellings, and the Ehgraben sewer, which reveals how a medieval town dealt with its waste and sewage problems.

reasons.text: An officially designated archaeological exhibition in the Old Town.
reasons.quote: However, a key is needed to visit the Ehgraben, Lindenhof-Keller, Stadtmauerkeller, and Brunngasse.

reasons.text: Archaeological and historical interpretation of the church and its medieval past.
reasons.quote: A multimedia exhibition in the crypt spans 1200 years of city and church history.

reasons.text: The church is a former medieval abbey.
reasons.quote: Not far from Paradeplatz, this church is known for its magnificent Chagall windows, but its history, too, is worth exploring.

reasons.text: Romanesque crypt and medieval ecclesiastical architecture.
reasons.quote: From archaeology to contemporary art: the Grossmünster fascinates with its Romanesque crypt, the Zurich Bible in the Scripture Collection and the stained-glass windows by Augusto Giacometti and Sigmar Polke.

reasons.text: The church's historical significance is accessible through guided tours.
reasons.quote: The rich history of the churches in the old town is made accessible to an interested public in regular guided tours.

reasons.text: One of Zurich's oldest public fountains, dating from approximately 1430.
reasons.quote: Er wurde vermutlich 1430 in Betrieb genommen.

reasons.text: An early example of a fountain regarded as public artwork as well as a functional water source.
reasons.quote: Bemerkenswert ist, dass der Amazonenbrunnen erstmals nicht nur der profanen Nutzung diente, sondern zugleich als öffentliches Kunstwerk betrachtet wurde.

reasons.text: The fountain is historically recognized as Zurich's first public running fountain.
reasons.quote: Der Rundgang führt vorbei am Amazonenbrunnen am Rennweg, der seit 1430 aktenkundig ist und als erster öffentlicher Laufbrunnen galt.

reasons.text: Historic fountain constructed in 1667.
reasons.quote: Er wurde im Jahr 1667 im Zusammenhang mit der Pumpanlage an der Limmat und dem an der Mauer stehenden Reservoirhäuschen gebaut.

reasons.text: The fountain features a historical female warrior figure associated with a Zurich legend dating from 1292.
reasons.quote: Die Figur von Gustav Siber (1864–1927) erinnert an die Legende der tapferen Zürcherinnen, die 1292 in Kampfmontur das Heer von Herzog Albrecht I. von Habsburg abschreckten, indem sie sich auf dem Lindenhof versammelten und so ein kampfkräftiges Heer vortäuschten.

reasons.text: A historic fountain and landmark in one of Zurich's most important historical locations.
reasons.quote: Der Brunnen auf dem Lindenhof hat eine bewegte Geschichte.

reasons.text: Historic fountain probably constructed in 1575.
reasons.quote: Der vermutlich 1575 errichtete Stüssibrunnen nimmt unter den zahlreichen alten Brunnen eine Sonderstellung ein: Als einziger Zürcher Brunnen ist er mehrfigurig.

reasons.text: The fountain's armoured figure may represent the medieval mayor Rudolf Stüssi.
reasons.quote: Ob die Figur tatsächlich den Rudolf Stüssi zeigt, der hier an der Hofstatt gewohnt und 1443 sein Leben im Alten Zürichkrieg verloren hat, ist umstritten.

reasons.text: The fountain has a connection to Swiss literature through Gottfried Keller.
reasons.quote: Durch Gottfried Kellers «Grünen Heinrich», wo Keller das Rauschen der nahen Limmat und das Plätschern des Brunnens schildert, gelangte der Stüssibrunnen in die Weltliteratur.

reasons.text: Historic fountain dating back to at least 1576.
reasons.quote: Seit 1576 stand der Brunnen über 300 Jahre lang vor dem mittelalterlichen Brunnenzentrum am Napfplatz.

reasons.text: The fountain occupies an historically important square in the medieval Old Town.
reasons.quote: Der Ort war ein bedeutender Altstadtplatz.

reasons.text: The fountain retains a sculptural figure dating from 1937.
reasons.quote: Die heutige Brunnenfigur stammt aus dem Jahr 1937.

reasons.text: The location had a simple wooden fountain trough as early as 1413.
reasons.quote: Der Hechtplatz war einst eine kleine Limmatbucht, wo sich bereits 1413 ein einfacher Holztrog befand.

reasons.text: The present fountain was constructed in 1760.
reasons.quote: Der heutige Brunnen entstand 1760.

reasons.text: The fountain is decorated with a sculptural figure of a young man observing a pike.
reasons.quote: Auf dem korinthischen Kapitell steht ein Jüngling, der seinen an Land gezogenen Hecht zufrieden betrachtet.

reasons.text: The fountain is documented historically from 1566.
reasons.quote: Der Herkulesbrunnen ist 1566 erstmals geschichtlich erwähnt.

reasons.text: Its distinctive architectural design differs from the commonly used baluster-column design of Swiss fountains.
reasons.quote: Von architektonischem Interesse ist, dass der Brunnen statt der in der Schweiz fast durchwegs üblichen Balustersäule einen mit Blattwerk profilierten Pfeiler aufweist.

reasons.text: The fountain has a distinctive sandstone pillar.
reasons.quote: Der Pfeiler wurde aus Sandstein aus Bargazoo gefertigt.

reasons.text: The fountain features a sculpture of the goddess Nike.
reasons.quote: Am Rindermarkt im Niederdorf erfährt man, warum auf dem Jupiterbrunnen die Göttin Nike thront.

reasons.text: It is included in the city's historical fountain tour, which introduces the cultural and historical significance of Zurich's fountains.
reasons.quote: Die Wasserversorgung möchte der Zürcher Bevölkerung auf einer Brunnentour Wissenswertes zur Geschichte und Kultur der Brunnen vermitteln.

reasons.text: The fountain was an emblem of the fishermen's guild in the 16th century.
reasons.quote: Die spannende Zeitreise bringt die Besucherinnen und Besucher aber auch auf die Stüssihofstatt zum einzigen mehrfarbigen Brunnen und an das Limmatquai zum Fischmarkt-/Samsonbrunnen, der im 16. Jahrhundert das Wahrzeichen der Fischerzunft darstellte.

reasons.text: The fountain is an important stop on the city's historical fountain tour.
reasons.quote: Abschluss: 19.30 Uhr Fischmarktbrunnen am Limmatquai 42

reasons.text: The fountain is part of Zurich's historic fountain heritage and is included in the city's historical fountain tour.
reasons.quote: Die spannende Zeitreise geht dann zum Fischmarkt-/Samsonbrunnen, der im 16. Jahrhundert das Wahrzeichen der Fischerzunft darstellte.

reasons.text: The Winzerbrunnen is specifically identified as a stop on the historical fountain route.
reasons.quote: Auf der anderen Limmatseite führt die Tour am Winzerbrunnen vorbei zum ersten öffentlichen Laufbrunnen.

reasons.text: The fountain dates from 1872 and depicts Juno, the Roman goddess of marriage and family.
reasons.quote: Juno, Gattin des Jupiters und Göttin der Ehe und der Familie, wurde von den Römern jeweils am 14. Februar geehrt.

reasons.text: The fountain has a documented nineteenth-century origin and underwent artistic restoration in 1995.
reasons.quote: Der Junobrunnen stammt aus dem Jahr 1872.

reasons.text: The fountain's sculptural figure and column were renewed by Zurich artists.
reasons.quote: 1995 erneuerte der Zürcher Bildhauer Romano Fenaroli die Figur und der Bildhauer Horst Bohnet die Brunnensäule.
